title_en: Inogrid launches ‘OpenStackIt 3.5’… Evolving into a virtualization platform that accommodates AI infrastructure
summary_en: [ZD Net Korea] Inogrid is introducing a cloud platform tailored to the rapidly changing corporate infrastructure environment as artificial intelligence (AI) is introduced in earnest. Inogrid announced on the 3rd that it has launched 'Openstackit 3.5', a private cloud platform that has advanced its own virtualization technology. Through this version, the company plans to lay the foundation to accommodate AI infrastructure beyond the existing virtualization infrastructure. OpenStackIt 3.5 reorganized the entire platform based on 'Gazpacho 2026.1', the latest version of OpenStack, and strengthened the core functions required for large-scale infrastructure operation. The most notable features are operation automation and resource optimization functions. It supports a maintenance mode that automatically moves VMs on servers that require maintenance to another node and restores them to their original location after the work is completed. In addition, the resource usage status of each compute node was analyzed and the function to relocate virtual machines (VMs) to the optimal location was strengthened to increase infrastructure utilization. The high availability function to ensure service stability was also advanced. title_en: Kolon Benit expands integrated management business ahead of mandatory ESG disclosure... Supports supply chain due diligence
summary_en: [GD Net Korea] Kolon Benit, an IT service affiliate of Kolon Group, is expanding its environmental, social, and governance (ESG) integrated management system business. The strategy is to combine SAP's ESG solution with its own supply chain due diligence solution to support everything from ESG data management to disclosure response and supply chain management. title_en: [Interview] Kim Hong-guk, CEO of Gabia, who appeared in the tender offer conflict... “Align, we only care about return on investment”
summary_en: [ZD Net Korea] CEO Kim Hong-guk, founder of Gabia, spoke directly about the controversy surrounding the tender offer by Macquarie Asset Management and the demand for board reorganization by activist fund Align Partners, a major shareholder. CEO Kim drew a line at the view of some that the deal with Macquarie was a choice to maintain management rights, and stated that it was a decision that took into consideration the continuity of long-term businesses, including Internet Data Center (IDC). On the other hand, he strongly criticized Align, saying that it is prioritizing investment returns over the company's main business and future growth. Gabia was founded in 1998 and established in 2005. It is an IT infrastructure company listed on KOSDAQ.
